# Mindmap Downstream Chart-Planning Obligations (Compiled Verbatim)

These obligations are extracted verbatim from this repository's downstream writing, tool, audit, linking, sitemap, and publication contracts so BUILD and CHART-REVIEW enforce every planning constraint without loading execution-only procedures. Execution workers (WRITE, AUDIT, PUBLISH) still load their full phase and standard files.

## [cs-tested-anchor-neutrality] (.claude/commands/_content-standard.md @ 944c2d85565a)

**Applies to** operator-register pages whose `page type:` is a roundup ("best X", "X alternatives", any ranked list), a product or model review, or an "X vs Y" comparison. **Skip** pricing, how-to, explainer, definition, tool and news (reporter-register) pages. **Also skip** any page whose ranked or compared items fall outside what this site's `_experience.md` section G licenses as tested (for example medical treatments, clinics, drugs, legal or financial services). If the site's `_experience.md` has no section G, skip TESTED entirely. Only relevant executed runs, independently reviewed against the exact page, license first-person testing claims; calculations, modeling, client observations and external research use their own accurate labels.

Plan an extra 3–5-row comparison table + "when to choose X" section (`COMPARISON` net-add) whenever a natural comparison axis exists; plan one honest proprietary `ANCHOR` from `_experience.md` / original analysis (max 2 named-client refs, or explicit `anchor-exempt:` justification — never force-fit); and never plan claims of vendor neutrality, "no paid placement", or self-undercutting disclaimers about what we have not tested or used (`NEUTRALITY`). Reuse this site's established author/publisher identity automatically without blocking on missing Person/reviewer profiles.

## [cs-seo-and-elements] (.claude/commands/_content-standard.md @ 944c2d85565a)

Every planned new page and substantive outline must budget for these required elements (in both `operator` and `reporter` registers unless noted):
- **50–60 char SEO title** carrying the primary keyword; Title Case H1/H2/H3 headings; sentence-case FAQ questions; define every acronym on first use; link related hub/spoke/cluster pages; no `Conclusion` or `Summary` heading.
- **Reader question & answer placement (INTENT):** decide `reader question: "<in the reader's words>"` with its PAA/autocomplete evidence tag (`[PAA n/m ...]` or `[verb-only ...]`), place the working answer in section 1 or 2 ahead of any scope/definition/history material, answer the top on-intent PAA in the opener, and place remaining on-topic PAA questions in the FAQ.
- **Who this is not for** and **What would change our answer** on any page that recommends, ranks, or picks a winner; **concrete next action** as the final body sentence; **disclaimers at the bottom only** (required on YMYL sites per `_experience.md`, never in title/intro/section 1); and a subject-specific `inlineCta` where the repo's page record supports one.

## [cs-medium-and-row-records] (.claude/commands/_content-standard.md @ 944c2d85565a)

Choose the useful deliverable from the actual reader finding and verified capabilities, following `_decision-evidence.md` and `_mindmap-execution.md`. Prose, finite tables, SVG charts, genuine screenshots, images/illustrations, downloadable data and interactive tools are supported when this run can actually produce them. Generated illustrations never establish product testing. Videos remain outside the Mindmap evidence workflow.

Record `medium: <picked> → <resolved>`, `register: operator|reporter`, and `page type: <type>` (from the DEPTH floor table: comparison 1,500 / review 1,500 / persona 1,400 / hub 1,200 / worth-it 1,200 / explainer 1,200 / cost-pricing 1,000 / editorial 600 body words; pick the higher floor when ambiguous, and merge topics too thin to clear their floor without filler). Assess inputs, logic, sources, implementation and feasibility before the approval chart. Prefer existing components and the smallest format that makes the answer useful. Keep the main answer readable without interaction.

Build the approved asset and its framing page in Phase 3 and independently audit both in Phase 4. A spec, stub, placeholder or promise that a human will build it later is not completion. If a requested format cannot be produced with available authorized capabilities, narrow/exclude that asset before approval, or resolve to a useful complete supported format. Do not force a calculator or visual when it adds nothing. Preserve local scope, exclusions and publication permissions.

## [cs-defend-lock] (.claude/commands/_content-standard.md @ 944c2d85565a)

**Before editing, rewriting, or appending to ANY existing page, check `reports/ai-answer-citation-pass/defended-pages.json` (if it exists in this repo).** If the page's route is listed in `pages[].route`, the page is **AIO-defended**: Google's AI Overview currently cites it as the source for its query, and rewriting it risks losing that citation.

- A defended route is **frozen** — do NOT rewrite, append to, or metadata-edit it. Skip it and log `skipped — AIO-defended` in your digest, exactly like a cooldown skip.
- The ONE exception: correcting a genuine factual error (e.g. a YMYL fact went stale). Such an edit still runs the full audit, and you note it so the next `/ai-answer-citation-pass` run re-checks the citation survived.

## [aal-outline-and-headline-bans] (.claude/commands/_anti-ai-language.md @ ed96c1f406eb)

Planned titles, working H1s, subtitles, and section outlines in Mindmap charts and new-page briefs must obey headline rules: never plan `Conclusion`, `Summary`, or `Final Thoughts` headings; never use coy abstractions where the subject name belongs (`the Vendor`, `the Platform`, `this Tool`); never presuppose reader ownership (`before you switch`, `your current system`) or prior state (`still`, `now`, `no longer`); avoid two-clause spliced headlines (`X: What It Is and How to Choose`, `X, and Why It Matters`), tricolons, em-dashes, `"honest"`, or `"actually"`/`"really"`/`"truly"`. Full prose tell checks run in WRITE and Phase 4 AUDIT.

## [rpa-prepare-answer-and-scope] (.claude/commands/_rendered-page-audit.md @ 5d3359c3235b)

Finish research needed for the proposed answer, setup instructions, pricing, product availability, comparisons and takeaway before marking preparation Passed. “Fetch/verify in Phase 3” is unfinished preparation when the source supports the proposed answer. Optional unsupported material must be explicitly excluded from the approved scope, not presented as planned content with a future verification condition. Missing paid metrics may retain the authorized labeled fallback. Keep one preparation summary row and every complete new-page brief. Enumerate every changed route and all routes affected by shared template/affiliate/link/date changes; test consequential conclusions against plausible primary-source counterexamples (source silence is not proof of a universal negative); and verify inherited “Tested and reviewed by” / “tested guidance” labels have real permitted evidence or plan their removal/narrowing.

## [p1-advisory-only] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-1-consolidation.md @ 0f599197b55b)

> ⚠️ **This phase no longer executes consolidation.** A backwards 301/canonical is the single most destructive action in SEO — a bot acting on partial GSC data can redirect the page Google actually ranks into a weaker one and crater a whole cluster. The *detection* (knowing two pages compete) is valuable; the *automated execution* is not. So this phase **only detects and flags** cannibalization for the human. It writes **no canonical, no 301, no body change, no link re-point, no sitemap removal.** Near-ties (within ~3×) must never be recommended for consolidation; differentiate angles (Phase 5) or add internal links (Phase 6) instead.

## [p2-metadata-gates-and-dates] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-2-metadata.md @ 22410042351d)

> **The title and description answer the reader's question, not the topic.** Where the chart row
> carries `reader_question` (cols 10–12, build-brief Step 4.6), the rewritten `metaTitle` and
> `metaDescription` must promise THAT answer in the reader's own words — a "how do I…" row gets a
> title that promises the method, a "how much" row promises the figure. Metadata rows touch ONLY head-level fields within discovered length limits, obey Gate 1 cooldown (`< 7` days hard defer; `7–21` days soft defer if `performing`; `>= 3` rewrites in 90d requires `>= 1,000` 30d GSC impressions), Gate 2 live GSC performance check (`performing` → defer), and Gate 3 top-impression query selection, and bump the rendered "Last updated" date + JSON-LD `dateModified` on every edited existing page.

## [p3-net-new-and-deliverables] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-3-new-content.md @ e2ba9e2aaa4f)

> **‼️ THE RUNNING AGENT DOES NOT WRITE THE ARTICLE.** Page prose (and substantive enrichments >1 sentence) is generated by the
> configured model through `scripts/lib/content_gen.py` per `.claude/commands/_content-generation.md`, using a closed verified fact list and allowed URL list, with `.meta.json` committed beside it (writer probes run only at actual writing steps, never on empty intakes).
> **Full-page creation is NET-NEW ONLY:** never overwrite, regenerate or replace an existing page as a new route (`create new content` pointing at an existing route → STOP and reclassify). Interactive tools/calculators/quizzes route to Phase 3c working builds; templates/glossaries/data reports/charts/downloads must be real built assets, never specs or stubs. On Layer3, check the durable reader-survey catalog/facts and apply `_layer3-evidence-sources.md` (anonymized client catalog + options 2/3 comparisons where useful; never publish client identities).

## [p3c-tool-feasibility] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-3c-tool-build.md @ d3f35f685d4f)

Phase 3 routes every `create new content` row whose format is `interactive tool`, `calculator` or
`quiz/assessment` here (plus approved tools embedded in existing articles). Planned tools must be BUILT in this run as client-side, deterministic components (`data-tool="<slug>"`, `<= ~30 KB gz`, no per-use paid API or new backend) mirroring an existing repo tool's wiring, with named sourced constants/formulas and result export/print where appropriate. If no defensible math or scoring exists, re-route the row to a normal article before approval — never ship a spec, stub, or invented math.

## [p4-request-and-audit-gate] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-4-audit.md @ 2bae3a5c4d34)

**Check the original request and actual presentation before applying the checklist.** Read the request artifact, its mapped requirements, approved action and presentation decision. Independently judge whether the rendered result delivers this action's share of the user's goal, rather than accepting a narrower writer brief as the whole request. Record `requestCoverage`, `presentationReview` and `caseUseReview` under `_mindmap-execution.md` with concrete evidence. Every planned substantive action (`create new content` or `update existing body text` / embedded tool) must map to the original request requirements, carry verifiable closed facts + allowed URLs, justify static vs interactive `presentation` where adjustable inputs could help, and clear its page-type depth floor without padding.

## [p5-enrichment-placement-and-monetization] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-5-body.md @ a6d4faa202c9)

**Where an `update existing body text` row carries `reader_question` / `answer` / `answer_placement` (cols 10–12), the added section IS that answer and goes in the named slot** — section 1 or 2, ahead of the page's existing scope/definition material, preserving unrelated content and bumping the rendered "Last updated" date + `dateModified`. Any addition longer than one sentence uses `content_gen.py section` with closed facts + `.meta.json`. Where the inline affiliate engine (`src/utils/affiliateInject.ts` + `data/affiliate/catalog.ts`) exists, plan natural-fit-only monetization (never force an off-intent block, double-monetize, or fabricate referral URLs).

## [p6-inbound-links-and-nav] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-6-internal-linking.md @ 9295f5f1fb5d)

> **Anchor text should match the destination's `reader_question` (chart col 10) where one exists.** Plan inbound internal links to every new Phase-3 page (**target ~3 links each** from genuinely relevant existing pages; relevance wins over count — 1–2 strong placements beat a forced link, and homepage header/nav is never touched, footer/body only) plus descriptive outbound internal links to related hubs/spokes (never `"click here"`). Bump rendered updated dates on existing pages edited for links per the repo's date-bump rule, without bumping sitemap `<lastmod>` on link-only touches.

## [p7-sitemap-and-indexnow-scope] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-7-sitemap-indexnow.md @ 03b378823a11)

Plan every new Phase-3 route for the correct discovered sitemap with today's `<lastmod>`, refresh `<lastmod>` ONLY for substantively changed pages (Phase 2/3/5 — never link-only Phase 6 touches), and prepare `<date>.indexnow.txt` for added + substantively updated canonical URLs while deferring actual IndexNow submission to Phase 9 after live verification.

## [p8-growth-and-cluster-accounting] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-8-summary.md @ 8b53826e4c1e)

For each substantive contribution, plan `growth.json` registration in `reports/content-evidence.jsonl` with a stable run/route ID, hypothesis, and honest baseline/comparator status (unavailable GSC is recorded as `unavailable`, never zero, and publishing is never claimed as uplift; respect terminal `no-addition` exemptions), plus complete accounting of emerging search clusters and PAA/completion vs `verb-only` question-evidence tags.

## [p9-publication-and-live-scope] (.claude/commands/mindmap-pass/phase-9-commit-deliver.md @ 8985b8609c57)

**Testing & live publication preparation:** Disclose explicit planned commit, default-branch land/push (or explicit local-only scope), host-provenance verification (`deployment-evidence.local.py` on Layer3 or `deployment-evidence.py` on fleet), exact `rendered-audit.py` live comparison across all affected and shared-template routes, `_testing-labels.md` adapter validation (blocking mismatched or unsupported leftover testing claims), and post-live canonical HTTP-200 IndexNow submission.

Read complete role-scoped applicable rules on the first visit. Do not pre-read `_workflow-efficiency.md`, `_workflow-checkpoints.md`, or role/phase files before `workflow-preflight.py prepare` — preflight compiles and delivers them automatically on Turn 1. Preflight compiles only byte-identical paragraphs once, preserves every original source hash and verifies complete delivery. Use `workflow-delivery-serial.local.py` for each unread part. Request up to TEN consecutive parts (`1..10`, then `11..20`, etc.) as SEPARATE Bash tool calls in one assistant message (fewer on the final turn). Each result contains one complete bounded part, and the final part automatically prints the dynamic Stage CLI Runbook so you never need `--help`/`grep`/`sed` on `.claude/tools/*.py`. Never concatenate, truncate or pipe instruction output. When constructing the `workflow-preflight.py check` application JSON, extract `>=30`-character verbatim substrings directly from `manifest['files']` via Python rather than grepping `.claude/tools/*.py`.

Keep the actual actor, phase, conversation and context epoch. Supply --context-id and --context-epoch to preflight prepare when using the portable protocol. Use --reuse only for this same role's completed reading in its actual uninterrupted context. Confirm in current words that rules remain accessible and understood and explain changed task application. Retain original explanations for unchanged instructions where an existing explanation protocol applies. New rules need reading and fresh explanations. Context loss, compaction or another worker requires a fresh reading. Independent reviewers retain their own context for corrections. No new per-document explanation gate is added.

The main conversation dispatches work only and never absorbs full phase bundles, drafts or rendered HTML into its own transcript. Fresh research (`BUILD`), independent `CHART-REVIEW`, `WRITE`, independent `AUDIT` and mechanical `PUBLISH` stages use the installed `mindmap-build`, `mindmap-chart-review`, `mindmap-write` and `mindmap-audit` stage agents and receive their role-scoped applicable instructions, original scope, current source evidence, latest candidate, unresolved findings and counters through sealed canonical job records (`workflow-handoff.py`). Do not poll subagent `.jsonl` transcripts after foreground `Agent` calls return. Keep old versions retrievable without loading whole conversations or superseded research. Preserve all original intake candidates and chart dispositions. Inspect structured `approval-manifest.json`, sealed handoff records and underlying source evidence directly (do not `cat` rendered Markdown charts in `WRITE`), and use batch CLI helpers (`mindmap-gates.py cases-batch`, batched prompt/allowed-URL setup, parallel `content_gen.py` invocations, batched data-file splicing + single lint pass, `rendered-audit.py capture-local --build`, `rendered-audit.py inspect-pack`, and `audit-batch.py reserve-batch`) rather than per-route shell loops or hand-rolled hash scripts. In `WRITE`, preserve existing `updatedDate` / `expectedUpdatedDate` on link-only Phase 6 edits (never bump dates when only adding inbound links), use structured `table` fields rather than raw Markdown `| col |` pipe rows inside `paragraphs[]`, and if cloud `node -v` is `< 20` when Next.js/Astro builds require Node 20+, prepend `/opt/nvm/versions/node/<v20>/bin` (or run `nvm install 20` once) before `npm run build` / `rendered-audit.py capture`.
